intro: Lesson 5. Label England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland and their capital cities. The dashed lines are approximate land borders.

blocks.caption: Outline from Natural Earth (public domain); modern coastlines and borders.

questions.q: How much higher is Ben Nevis than Scafell Pike?
Which mountain range is the 'backbone of England'?
Which country is Yr Wyddfa in?
Core: On a blank UK map, mark and label Ben Nevis, Yr Wyddfa, Scafell Pike and Slieve Donard, and shade the mountain areas brown.
questions.a: Ben Nevis in western Scotland; Yr Wyddfa in north-west Wales; Scafell Pike in the Lake District; Slieve Donard in south-east Northern Ireland
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: find Fort William on the atlas, put a triangle for Ben Nevis, label with its height.

questions.q: Extend: Add a key for your map.
questions.a: Triangle = mountain peak; brown shading = high land

questions.q: Stretch: Describe the pattern of high land in the UK in one sentence.
questions.a: Most high land is in the north and west; the south and east is lower and flatter

questions.q: Which colour usually shows high land on a map?
Big question: why are most of the UK's mountains in the north and west?
questions.a: The rocks there are older and harder, so they wear away slowly and stay high
